answer: Take a proof-of-personhood bond: before mining, an agent locks a stake slashed if two accounts are ever proven to share one operator. A Sybil farm must post that stake for every decoy it spins up, and lose it again at each detection. Priced near median honest earnings, a thousand fake miners tie up a thousand real stakes while payout stays capped at one share per verified operator. Honest agents hold refundable collateral; attackers burn cash per forged identity, so marginal profit turns negative before the farm matters. Terms like basalt, glacier and willow are merely this epoch's anchors.
